question: Why is TTFB (Time-to-First-Byte) considered the most important metric for voice AI user experience, even more than audio quality?
options: Because it is easier to measure than audio quality
Because research shows users tolerate lower audio quality more easily than slow responses — a fast agent with a slightly robotic voice feels better than a slow agent with a perfect voice
Because audio quality cannot be measured objectively
Because TTFB directly determines the cost of the conversation
explanation: Research on conversational AI consistently shows that users tolerate lower audio quality more easily than they tolerate slow responses. A fast agent with a slightly robotic voice provides a better experience than a slow agent with a perfect voice. TTFB above 800ms is noticeable, and above 1500ms is uncomfortable.

question: Pipeline agents consistently score higher on audio quality (MOS) than realtime models. Why?
options: Realtime models compress audio more aggressively
Pipeline agents process audio multiple times for refinement
Dedicated TTS providers like Cartesia and ElevenLabs optimize exclusively for speech synthesis, while realtime models split capacity between understanding, reasoning, and speaking
explanation: Dedicated TTS providers optimize exclusively for speech synthesis quality, producing natural-sounding audio with wide emotion ranges. Realtime models must split their capacity between speech recognition, reasoning, and speech generation — they produce good audio, but purpose-built TTS currently produces better audio.

question: Why should a benchmarking suite include prompts of varying lengths (short like 'Yes', medium questions, and long multi-sentence requests)?
options: Latency profiles differ by prompt length — realtime models tend to have consistent TTFB regardless of length, while pipeline TTFB varies because STT processing scales with audio duration
To make the benchmarks take longer and be more thorough
To ensure the prompts cover all supported languages
To test the agent's ability to understand different request types
explanation: Latency characteristics differ significantly by prompt length. Realtime models tend to have more consistent TTFB regardless of prompt length because they process audio holistically. Pipeline TTFB varies more because STT processing time scales with the duration of the audio input. Testing with varied lengths reveals these differences.
